motion: Prospective global warming is the most pressing issue facing humanity today and to avert it the world must de-carbonize its economies in short order.

dropped_turns.speaker: PRO
dropped_turns.text: Steady emissions cuts are better than doing nothing, and adaptation has a role. Yet gradual promises fail when carbon keeps accumulating, so the main task is urgent economy-wide decarbonization before harms outrun our ability to respond.

turns.speaker: MOD

Each has thirty seconds to open, followed by two and a half minutes of crossfire, then thirty-second closings. I will give a ten-second cue. We will keep the exchange focused and respectful.

turns.speaker: PRO
turns.text: Global warming is not a distant concern; it shapes food, shelter, health, and safety at once. Because emissions linger, delay locks in damage that later choices cannot easily undo. Decarbonizing quickly means building cleaner power, transport, and homes while protecting workers. The question is whether we act before those risks harden.

turns.speaker: MOD

turns.speaker: CON
turns.text: The climate matters, and reducing pollution can bring real benefits. But calling one future threat humanity's most pressing issue erases urgent present needs: hunger, conflict, illness, and insecure livelihoods. A forced rush away from carbon can raise energy costs and weaken fragile communities. Good policy weighs tradeoffs, lets people choose paths, and refuses to make one goal the sole test of progress.

turns.speaker: MOD
turns.text: You have ten seconds.

turns.speaker: CON
turns.text: We should innovate and cut emissions where it helps, but no universal timetable fits every economy. The resolution demands exactly that, so it goes too far.

turns.speaker: CON
turns.text: Cleaner power can improve local air, and I welcome that benefit. But the resolution makes warming the top priority over every immediate human need and demands a rushed global cure, which is false.

turns.speaker: PRO
turns.text: When a community can replace dirty power without losing basic reliability, rapid decarbonization is the responsible course. Those conditions can be created through planning and shared support, because unchecked warming makes every other need harder to meet.

turns.speaker: CON

turns.speaker: PRO
turns.text: Protecting people is precisely why decarbonization cannot be postponed. A warming world strips families of crops, safe homes, and stable prices, so the broad duty is to replace carbon rather than defend it.

turns.speaker: CON
turns.text: No economy should ever be forced to decarbonize. People need secure energy and control over their livelihoods, so persuasion and invention are better than a global order that commands sacrifice.

turns.speaker: PRO
turns.text: A plan that leaves families cold is not the plan I support; the premise is false. Fast decarbonization must provide dependable energy, while your voluntary approach lets the damage and costs keep spreading.

turns.speaker: CON
turns.text: A coal-bound island economy should be forced to decarbonize. Its leaders may cling to fuel, but residents facing rising water deserve outside action, even though the resolution still overreaches globally.

turns.speaker: CON
turns.text: I oppose a universal command, and I support action for that island economy because its crisis is immediate and shared. Those views fit: broad coercion is wrong, while collective rescue can answer a clear danger.

turns.speaker: PRO
turns.text: You say each society should choose its pace, but what do you offer people whose homes become unsafe while leaders delay? Is their safety less urgent than protecting carbon industries from change?

turns.speaker: CON
turns.text: On your point about unsafe homes, I reject the claim that carbon policy is their only protection. Strong housing, emergency planning, and affordable energy can protect people now without declaring forced decarbonization humanity's supreme duty.

turns.speaker: PRO
turns.text: Rod says people need reliable energy, and they do. But reliable energy on a damaged planet is not security; delaying transition deepens risks to homes, food, and work. Build clean systems fairly and quickly, because warming touches every human priority and demands first place.

turns.speaker: CON
turns.text: Betsy rightly wants people protected, but the resolution turns a serious danger into a single command for every society.
